div.head: VIIa Atr Prol.
div.ab: Ealle we beþurfan, þæt we geornlice earnian, þæt we Godes miltse ⁊ his mildheortnesse habban moton ⁊ þæt we þurh his fultum magon feondum wiðstandan.
Ealle we beþurfan þæt we geornlice earnian þæt we Godes miltse ⁊ his mildheortnesse habban moton ⁊ þæt we þurh his fultum magon feondum wiðstandan.

Ðis man gerædde, ða se micele here com to lande: Ealle we beþurfan þæt we geornlice earnian þæt we Godes miltse and his mildheortnesse habban moton and þæt we, þurh his fultum, magon feondum wiðstandan.
All of us have need to strive earnestly that we may obtain the mercy and compassion of God and through his help withstand our foes.
This was decreed when the great army came to this land: We all must strive diligently so that we may receive God’s mercy and compassion and, with his help, withstand our enemies.
All of us have need eagerly to labour that we may obtain God’s mercy and his compassion and that we may be able through his help to withstand our enemies.
Prol. Alle haben wir nöthig, dass wir eifrig [das] verdienen, dass wir Gottes Gnade und seine Barmherzigkeit erlangen können und dass wir durch seine Hilfe den Feinden zu widerstehen vermögen.
Prologue. We all need to strive eagerly to earn God's mercy and his compassion, and to be able, through his help, to withstand our enemies.
div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.
Manuscripts: D = Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 201, p. 30.

[title] This was decreed . . . land: The title likely refers to the invasion of the Viking “great army” under the leadership of Thurkil the Tall in 1009, the year in which the Latin version of 7 Æthelred was composed.
